newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. still pushing Infotech vision at APEC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. still pushing Infotech vision at APEC.

text.p: The United States is still pushing its vision of free trade in computer and telecommunications technolgy in meetings between President Bill Clinton and other Asia-Pacific leaders, an APEC official said on Sunday.
"Discussions are going on and it's at rather a sensitive stage," Philippine Foreign Affairs Undersecretary Rodolfo Severino told a news briefing.

Severino said Clinton and Philippine President Fidel Ramos had discussed the U.S. proposal for an Information Technology Agreement (ITA) during a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the annual meeting here of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
Officials indicated that Clinton had raised the subject.
Asked at what level ITA discussions were continuing, Severino said: "It's going on bilaterally."

"Now things are going on so an acceptable formulation can be included in the leaders' statement," he said. The statement will be issued after the leaders' summit in Subic Bay, north of Manila, on Monday.
Other officials said leaders were mulling whether to mention the contentious subject at all in their summit-ending statement.

The United States had been seeking APEC backing for its proposal for zero tariffs on computer and telecommunications technology and equipment by the year 2000 to take to a meeting of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Singapore next month.
But Washington only got a watered-down expression of support in a statement issued on Saturday after a two-day gathering of APEC foreign and trade ministers.

The ministers said in the statement they "endorsed the efforts at WTO to conclude an information technology agreement by the Singapore Ministerial Conference and urged all other members of the WTO to work toward that end".
The United States says the information technology business is worth at least $1 trillion a year, with 80 percent of that in the booming Asia-Pacific region.
